extracted.intended_audience: Citizens, framers, lawmakers, and readers interested in constitutional design and the proper distribution of governmental powers (late-18th-century American public).
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical principles for structuring a constitutionally free government by distributing legislative, executive, and judicial powers and providing mutual constitutional checks so no single department can accumulate whole powers of another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid accumulation of all powers in same hands
rubrics_metrics.description: The accumulation of all powers, legislative, executive, and judiciary, in the same hands, whether of one, a few, or many ... may justly be pronounced the very definition of tyranny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the whole power of one department is exercised by the same hands which possess the whole power of another, the fundamental principles of a free constitution are subverted. Prevent any single person or body from exercising the entire powers of another department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation does not require absolute independence of departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Montesquieu's maxim does not mean that these departments ought to have no PARTIAL AGENCY in, or no CONTROL over, the acts of each other; it means that the WHOLE power of one department must not be in the hands of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial agency and controls (appointments, vetoes, impeachment, consultative roles) are acceptable and historically present in the British and several State constitutions; the key is avoiding consolidation of whole powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constitutional mutual controls (blend enough to allow checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless these departments be so far connected and blended as to give to each a constitutional control over the others, the degree of separation required for free government can never in practice be duly maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions so each department has constitutional means to check encroachments by others (e.g., appointment/removal processes, impeachment, vetoes, appellate jurisdiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parchment boundaries are insufficient—need practical securities
rubrics_metrics.description: Will it be sufficient to mark, with precision, the boundaries of these departments, in the constitution, and to trust to these parchment barriers against the encroaching spirit of power? Experience assures us that the efficacy of the provision has been greatly overrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on written demarcations; incorporate structural, procedural, and incentive-based safeguards that operate in practice to restrain encroachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard particularly against legislative aggrandizement
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative department derives a superiority … Its constitutional powers being at once more extensive, and less susceptible of precise limits, it can ... mask encroachments ... It alone has access to the pockets of the people ... creating dependence in the other departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the legislative tendency to expand; adopt measures (fixed judicial salaries, limitations on legislative reach, procedural protections) to prevent lawmaking power from subsuming executive or judicial functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making other branches dependent on the legislature for subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: The judiciary and the executive members were left dependent on the legislative for their subsistence in office, and some of them for their continuance in it. If the legislature assumes executive and judiciary powers, no opposition is likely to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure appointment, tenure, and remuneration so the executive and judiciary are not subject to legislative control over their continuance or pay, reducing incentives to submit to legislative usurpation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain certain cross-departmental powers, but limit their scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive magistrate may have a qualified negative on the legislative body; the Senate may be a court of impeachment; the judges are appointable by the executive; yet none of the entire departments exercise the whole powers of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow limited, well-defined cross-functions (vetoes, impeachment trials, appointments) as checks, but restrict them so they cannot produce consolidation of whole departmental authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appeal-to-people (constitutional conventions) only for extraordinary cases
rubrics_metrics.description: As the people are the only legitimate fountain of power ... it seems consonant to recur to the same original authority ... whenever any one of the departments may commit encroachments on the chartered authorities of the others. But there are insuperable objections against recurrence to the people in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a constitutional road to appeal to the people for great and extraordinary occasions, but avoid frequent recourse which can destabilize government and erode reverence for institutions or be ineffective if two departments collude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits of popular conventions as remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the people does not reach the case of a combination of two of the departments against the third ... frequent appeals would ... deprive the government of that veneration which time bestows ... and would interest the public passions, disturbing public tranquillity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design remedies for encroachments that do not rely solely on popular conventions—include internal constitutional checks and institutional remedies sufficient to address collusion and avoid unnecessary agitation of public passions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve procedural and substantive constitutional safeguards (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council of Censors found that laws had been passed violating the rule that all bills of a public nature shall be previously printed; constitutional trial by jury had been violated; salaries of judges, which the constitution expressly requires to be fixed, had been occasionally varied; executive powers had been usurped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure concrete safeguards in the constitution and practice—prior publication of bills, protection of trial by jury, fixed judicial salaries, clear allocation of jurisdiction—to prevent legislative encroachment and preserve department integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for differences in departmental vulnerability by institutional form
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive department of Pennsylvania is distinguished by the number of members composing it. Being at once exempt from the restraint of an individual responsibility ... unauthorized measures would, of course, be more freely hazarded than where the executive is administered by a single hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select institutional forms (single vs. multi-member executive, selection methods) mindful of how structure affects susceptibility to unconstitutional acts and how it interacts with checks from other departments.
